_comment: Real payloads from Finnhub GET /stock/financials-reported?symbol=JNJ&freq=quarterly (2026-07-18). JNJ's fiscal year starts in January, so quarter=1 YTD values equal the isolated quarter (no decumulation needed); quarter=2/3 YTD values must be decumulated against the prior quarter in the same fiscal year.

alpha_vantage_reference._comment: Same 4 fiscalDateEnding values, raw single-quarter figures from Alpha Vantage INCOME_STATEMENT/CASH_FLOW (already in DB / used by build_quarterly_fundamentals) — for comparison against expected_isolated, NOT part of the decumulation logic under test.

balance_sheet._comment: Balance sheet items are point-in-time BALANCES, not period flows: no YTD accumulation exists for them in either source (unlike revenue/net_income/ocf/capex above), so no decumulation is needed — verified below by comparing raw Finnhub bs values directly against Alpha Vantage BALANCE_SHEET for the same 4 fiscalDateEnding.

debt_to_ebitda_impact._comment: First pass (isolation test): ebitda_ttm backed out from the debt_to_ebitda already stored in Supabase (fundamentals.debt_to_ebitda, 100% Alpha Vantage) for these 4 report_dates, using debt=short+long, cash as above. Since Finnhub's debt/cash are bit-identical to Alpha Vantage's (see balance_sheet above), recomputing debt_to_ebitda with Finnhub-sourced debt/cash (same ebitda_ttm, untouched) yields the identical ratio and therefore an identical normalized score component — 0.00 point difference on the final fundamental_score for JNJ on these 4 quarters. See debt_to_ebitda_hybrid_real below for the ACTUAL prod-shape combination (debt/cash from AV, EBITDA from Finnhub).

debt_to_ebitda_hybrid_real._comment: The REAL prod-shape hybrid: debt/cash from Alpha Vantage (default source, unchanged), EBITDA_TTM from Finnhub's own stock/metric quarterly 'ebitda' series (4-quarter sum, real values below — NOT backed out from the stored ratio like the first pass above). ebitda_ttm_finnhub is consistently ~1.7-2.4% BELOW the Alpha-Vantage-derived ebitda_ttm for JNJ — well under the 5% tolerance. Resulting debt_to_ebitda and normalized score differ by <0.01 in the ratio and <0.1 point (out of 100, weight 0.15) in the final score.

fiscal_date_gap_multi_ticker._comment: AV fiscalDateEnding (always a calendar quarter-end) vs Finnhub endDate (actual reporting-period end), 6 quarters each, real payloads (2026-07-18). Confirms gap_days is NOT stable across fiscal calendars: 0 for MSFT (calendar fiscal year, exact match every quarter), 1-2 for JNJ, up to 4 for AAPL (4-4-5 retail calendar). The existing 5-day tolerance (finnhub_client.FISCAL_DATE_TOLERANCE_DAYS) covers the observed worst case (AAPL, 4 days) with a 1-day margin — kept as-is, not widened without evidence.

revenue_net_income_fallback_rate_5y._comment: Measured, not theoretical: for each ticker's real Alpha Vantage fiscalDateEnding list over the last 5 years, checked whether a Finnhub isolated (decumulated) quarter exists within fiscal_date_match tolerance. Confirms the fallback rate exceeds the ~25% Q4-only floor — extra Finnhub financials-reported filing-coverage gaps exist beyond the structural Q4/10-K exclusion (e.g. JNJ's 2024-Q2 filing is simply absent from financials-reported). No Alpha Vantage request is ever skipped regardless (see finnhub_client.py module docstring) — this only measures how often the revenue/net_income VALUE substitution itself succeeds.

debt_cash_conditional_balance_sheet_anal._comment: Per-quarter debt/cash fiscal_date_match success rate (~67% match / ~33% fallback, same order as revenue/net_income; JNJ's ShortTermBorrowings tag doesn't exist for AAPL/MSFT, which use LongTermDebtCurrent instead — a real XBRL-taxonomy variance across tickers, not just a date-alignment issue). BUT: Alpha Vantage's BALANCE_SHEET endpoint returns ALL quarters in ONE call — it cannot be fetched per-quarter. build_quarterly_fundamentals rebuilds the FULL 5-year/20-quarter history on every refresh (no incremental-quarter-only mode exists). Making debt/cash Finnhub-primary therefore does NOT let BALANCE_SHEET be skipped in proportion to the ~67% per-quarter match rate: the call is only skippable when ALL ~20 quarters in the window match, which never happened on any of the 3 real tickers tested (each already has >=6 fallback quarters in its own window) and has a theoretical probability of ~0.67^20 =~ 0.02% even under an aggregate rate. REAL measured gain: 0/3 tickers could have skipped BALANCE_SHEET -> 0% (not the naively-expected ~67%). Verdict: NOT implemented (well under the 30% threshold) -- see finnhub_client.py module docstring.

overview_field_audit._comment: Quick inventory only (Task 3, no dedicated validation round). Fields actually read from Alpha Vantage OVERVIEW in fetch.py (grep-verified, 2026: only 5 fields, NOT market_cap/pe/ebitda_ttm as one might assume -- those are computed elsewhere from BALANCE_SHEET/price data): Symbol (validity check), Name, Sector, Industry, Currency.

finnhub_equivalent.Symbol: stock/profile2.ticker -- exact equivalent, no extra endpoint needed
finnhub_equivalent.Name: stock/profile2.name -- exact equivalent
finnhub_equivalent.Sector: stock/profile2.finnhubIndustry -- approximate only: Finnhub's own single-level industry classification, not AV's GICS-style Sector taxonomy -- would need a mapping table and its own validation round
finnhub_equivalent.Industry: no free equivalent found in profile2 or stock/metric -- AV's finer-grained Industry has no Finnhub match without a premium endpoint

overview_field_audit.verdict: 3 of 5 fields (Symbol, Name, Currency) are clean 1:1 substitutes already available via the profile2 call made during the earlier IP-reachability test -- no new endpoint required. Sector needs a mapping/validation pass. Industry has no known free equivalent. Given OVERVIEW is just 1 of 7 Alpha Vantage requests/ticker and none of BALANCE_SHEET/CASH_FLOW/EARNINGS/INCOME_STATEMENT depend on it, migrating it would save at most 1/7 (~14%) of Alpha Vantage requests -- worth a dedicated round only if that's judged worthwhile later; not pursued here.

revenue_net_income_tag_coverage._comment: Real revenue/net_income XBRL concepts observed across 9 tickers spanning 6 sectors (tech: AAPL/MSFT; pharma: JNJ/LLY; banking: JPM; payments: V; managed-care/health-insurance: UNH; energy: XOM; REIT: O), from financials-reported?freq=quarterly payloads. Basis for the ordered candidate lists in finnhub_client.py (_REVENUE_CONCEPTS / _NET_INCOME_CONCEPTS).

revenue: us-gaap_PrincipalTransactionsRevenue (partial line item, NOT total revenue)
us-gaap_RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense (verified ~34% below Alpha Vantage totalRevenue -- excluded on purpose)

net_income: MISSING from Finnhub's ic section on most recent quarters -- genuine Finnhub data gap, not a tag-name mismatch

revenue: us-gaap_RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax (WRONG for this ticker -- only ~20% of total, insurance premiums are out of ASC 606 scope by GAAP definition, a real accounting nuance for health-plan/insurance issuers)
xom_TotalRevenuesAndOtherIncome (company-specific extension, not in candidate list)
us-gaap_OperatingLeasesIncomeStatementLeaseRevenue (REIT-specific partial line item, not in candidate list)

revenue_net_income_tag_coverage.deliberately_excluded: JPM's bank-specific revenue tags (PrincipalTransactionsRevenue, InvestmentBankingRevenue, RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense) -- RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense measured ~34% below Alpha Vantage's totalRevenue for JPM, consistently every quarter (not an erratic jump a magnitude-vs-prior-quarter check would catch) -- financial-sector revenue stays a permanent, legitimate Alpha Vantage fallback, same treatment as ebitda_ttm's bank non-coverage.

revenue_net_income_coverage_v2._comment: Re-measured with the multi-tag candidate list + magnitude-consistency guard (vs the single-hardcoded-tag round that scored 0% on LLY/JPM/V). Method unchanged: decumulated Finnhub value vs Alpha Vantage's own same-quarter value, 5-year window, magnitude_consistent() = within 25%. 7 tickers with real Alpha Vantage ground truth (JNJ/AAPL/MSFT from earlier fixtures + LLY/JPM/V/UNH from the live 2026-07-18 production run's Supabase data) -- XOM/O have no Alpha Vantage data yet (not backfilled) so are excluded from this measurement (tag-availability only, see revenue_net_income_tag_coverage above).

JPM.note: revenue=0 BY DESIGN (bank revenue tags excluded, see deliberately_excluded above), not a bug

V.note: net_income=0: Finnhub's ic section genuinely lacks any net-income tag on most recent V filings -- a real data gap, not a matching failure

UNH.note: revenue=2/20: the magnitude guard correctly rejects RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax for UNH (only ~20% of true revenue -- insurance premiums are out of ASC 606 scope) on the other 18 quarters, falling back to Alpha Vantage every time -- the guard is working as intended, the underlying tag priority just isn't optimal for this sector

comparison_to_prior_rounds.round_1_single_tag_3_tickers_tech_pharma: ~65-68% (JNJ/AAPL/MSFT only -- happened to share compatible tags)
comparison_to_prior_rounds.round_2_single_tag_3_new_tickers: 0% (LLY/JPM/V -- each used a different/incompatible tag, exposing the hardcoded-single-tag design flaw)
comparison_to_prior_rounds.round_3_multi_tag_7_tickers_6_sectors: ~50-58% (this measurement) -- lower than round 1's number because it includes GENUINE non-coverage (bank revenue, V's missing net-income tag, UNH's ASC-606 scope nuance), not because the multi-tag fix regressed anything: JNJ/AAPL/MSFT's own individual rates are unchanged or improved, LLY/JPM(net_income) went from 0% to 70-74%/60%.

revenue_net_income_coverage_v2.confidence_caveat: Based on 7 tickers across 6 sectors -- informative directional signal, NOT a statistically robust estimate for a ~26-ticker (growing) portfolio. Real coverage on the actual portfolio (mostly tech, some industrials/healthcare/comm. services, no banking/REIT/energy backfilled yet) is more likely to sit toward the higher end (60-70%) given the current sector mix, but this should be re-confirmed once XOM (energy, already queued) and any future financial-sector ticker are actually backfilled with Alpha Vantage data.
